name: covered
behaviour: The page has the screen covered (launch intro, CONNECTING, gate screen): native takes the splash and the app-switcher cover down. Nothing is read from the message. Sent on every gate screen, twice per showing is normal.
timing: Before the 8 s splash backstop. Native treats a second one as no news.

name: log
behaviour: Every console.log/warn/error of the page, mirrored in every build (mirrorConsole). Native writes it to its log; in Release iOS print() reaches only FieldLog, which redacts tokens, invoices, payment requests, onion addresses, keys and long hex on the way in.

name: fieldLog
behaviour: The ERRORS (bad=true) and LOGS screens: native and page lines, redacted, newest last.

name: fieldLogClear
behaviour: Forgets every FieldLog line.

name: isDebug
behaviour: Whether this is a debug build. Served, but nothing in the page at the pinned commit asks it: the page reads window.FOXY_DEBUG, injected at document start.

name: awake
behaviour: Hold the screen lit while a screen is looked at rather than touched (an invoice held up, the gate). Released by native whenever the app leaves the foreground.

name: captured
behaviour: Whether the screen is being recorded or mirrored right now, for a page that starts while it already is; changes are pushed with _captured.

name: privacy

p1.why: No Tor in P1: the snapshot a build without Tor answers (Route.snapshot, the #else branch), so the gate shows CANNOT CONNECT TO TOR.

behaviour: Reads the route snapshot (Route.snapshot). The same object is pushed with _privacy on every change.

name: torRetry

p1.why: Nothing to restart: the same no-Tor snapshot as privacy.

behaviour: RETRY / RESTART TOR: a full Tor restart (TorService.restart), answered with the snapshot.

name: unprotected

p1.why: The unprotected path is not built until P2 (ROUTE.md): on is ignored, and the no-Tor snapshot answers.

behaviour: CONTINUE WITHOUT TOR. on=true asks a native alert ("Continue without Tor?") that no script can answer, and is ignored while Tor is running; on=false clears it with no question. Session only; Tor connecting clears it. Pushes _privacy and answers the snapshot.
timing: The page waits up to 600 s for an on=true answer (a person is reading an alert).

name: orbotRefresh

p1.why: No Orbot link on Android yet (ANDROID-MAPPING decision 3): Orbot is reported as none.

behaviour: Poll Orbot now instead of on its 15 s timer; answers OrbotLink.name.

name: orbotAccess

p1.why: No Orbot link on Android yet (ANDROID-MAPPING decision 3): nothing is opened.

behaviour: Opens Orbot's own permission flow for a key with bypass.

name: mintRequest

p1.error: Foxy is not connected to Tor.
p1.why: Route.available is false in P1 (ROUTE.md): the refusal, nothing contacted.

errors: That is not a mint address Foxy will use.
That is not a request Foxy will send.
Foxy is not connected to Tor.
You did not allow Foxy to contact <host>.
The answer from <host> was too large.
An .onion address needs Tor, and Foxy is not connected to Tor.
<host> could not be asked over Tor: <why>
Foxy's private connection was rebuilt mid-request. Try again.

behaviour: Every mint, LNURL / lightning-address and block-explorer request the page makes (cashu-ts customRequest, nativeRequest). In order: url parses; Route.urlProblem (https, or http to .onion; no localhost, IP literal, single label, .local family; .onion needs Tor); method GET or POST only; Route.available or the refusal; HostApprovals (an unknown host is asked about in a native alert first); then sent on the Tor circuit labelled `circuit` (16-64 lowercase hex, else a fresh one). Only content-type and accept headers are passed; generic Tor-Browser User-Agent. Plain http to an .onion goes through Tor SOCKS by hand (GET only). Answer capped at 4 MB. Redirects re-checked and never to another host. NSURLErrorBadURL retried once after 0.4 s.
timing: The page waits 65 s. A swap/melt/mint/restore POST is counted in moneyInFlight so backgrounding waits up to 20 s for it.

name: price

p1.error: Foxy is not connected to Tor.
p1.why: Route.available is false in P1 (ROUTE.md): the refusal, nothing contacted.

errors: Foxy is not connected to Tor.
no price source answered
the price sources did not agree
reply.note: USD per BTC as a decimal string; "" with an error when none answered

behaviour: BTC/USD from six operators in order (mempool onion, Kraken, Bitstamp, blockchain.info, Gemini, Coinbase), two at a time, first usable answer wins; agree=true needs two within 2% (a payment typed in dollars). 4 s per source direct, 20 s on a bridge, 10/25 s for the onion; whole walk 12/30 s (25/45 s with agree).
timing: Page waits 14 s (34 s bridged; 29/49 s with agree).

name: candles

p1.error: Foxy is not connected to Tor.
p1.why: Route.available is false in P1 (ROUTE.md): the refusal, nothing contacted.

reply.items: array of [unixSeconds, close] number pairs, oldest first
errors: Foxy is not connected to Tor.
unreadable candles
could not encode candles

behaviour: Chart history from Kraken OHLC, interval chosen from the fixed set so the range fits 720 candles. g clamped to 60..86400 s, span to 3600 s..4 years.
timing: Page waits 16 s; native times the request out at 12 s.

name: hostsKnown

p1.why: No host approvals until P2, so nothing to carry over.

behaviour: Once, the first time a version with host approvals runs: the mints and contact domains the wallet already used are carried over as approved (each approves only itself). Later calls change nothing.

name: seedStatus

errors: the seed could not be read

behaviour: Whether a seed is saved. quiet=true answers from presence alone (no biometric prompt); without it the seed is read (may prompt). "passcode": false only on a phone with no device credential. Finding a seed closes the seedMigrate window.

name: seedCreate

errors: a seed already exists
the seed could not be read
the wordlist could not be checked
the seed could not be made
Another change to the seed is still waiting. Nothing was changed.

behaviour: Twelve words made natively (128 bits from the platform CSPRNG, the bundled wordlist used only if its SHA-256 is pinned) and saved; never replaces a saved seed; counters left from a gone seed are moved aside first. One seed change at a time.

name: seedMigrate

errors: bad request
no migration here
the wordlist could not be checked
Another change to the seed is still waiting. Nothing was changed.

behaviour: The one-time move of words a pre-keychain page still holds (localStorage foxy.seed.v1). Only a valid BIP-39 phrase (<=1000 bytes, or <=24 words), written only inside the one-time window and only where no seed is saved; otherwise same/different, changing nothing. Never answers words.

name: countersImport

errors: bad request
counters were already imported
too many keysets

behaviour: Once per install: the page's old NUT-13 counters ({keysetId: next}) raised into the native file (max of each). At most 256 keysets.

name: counterReserve

errors: bad request
no seed
the seed could not be read
too many keysets
outside the keyset's counters

behaviour: Reserve `count` (0..1000) counters for a 00/01 keyset and answer their NUT-13 secrets and blinding factors (hex). The range is written to the counter file BEFORE the secrets are answered. count=0 is a peek: answers start=next with empty lists and needs no seed.

name: counterReserveAt

errors: bad request
range already issued
too far ahead
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: Reserve an explicit range: refused if it starts below next (already issued) or more than 100 past it.

name: counterAdvance

errors: bad request
too far ahead

behaviour: Move a counter up, never down; at most 100 past next, or to the end of a range restoreSecrets served this session.

name: counterSnapshot
behaviour: Reads every keyset's next counter; moves nothing; needs no seed.

name: restoreSecrets

errors: bad request
outside the restore window
unknown candidate
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: Secrets for a restore scan, moving no counter: for the saved seed only ranges ending at most 1000 past next; for a typed-words candidate (seedEnter) contiguously from 0 up to 20000. Notes the furthest range served (counterAdvance may reach it; seedAdopt raises counters to 1000 short of it).

name: p2pkReserve

errors: bad request
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: Reserve 0..64 lock-key indexes on NUT-13's P2PK path m/129373'/10'/0'/0'/i (last level normal) and answer their compressed PUBLIC keys; the index is written first. count=0 is a peek.

name: p2pkPubkeys

errors: bad request
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: Public keys only, 1..300 at a time, no index past 20000; moves nothing but notes the scan's reach (which p2pkKey may then answer).

name: p2pkKey

errors: bad request
outside the lock-key window
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: One lock key's private half, only within 1000 of the last index reserved or inside a range this session's scan served. The chain code is never answered.

name: seedShow

errors: a seed screen is already open
try again in a moment
no seed
the seed could not be read
Nothing to present the screen from.

behaviour: Native screen showing the words (behind biometric/device credential), with the verify quiz when verify=true. Answers only whether the quiz was finished, whether delete was asked, whether the words were revealed. One seed screen at a time; none within 10 s of a cancelled read. A cancelled/closed screen answers {"verified": false}.

name: seedEnter

errors: a seed screen is already open
too many candidates
cancelled
the words could not be read
the wordlist could not be checked
Nothing to present the screen from.

behaviour: Native screen where the person types words to restore. Answers a random 128-bit candidate id, never the words. Two candidates at most, dropped on unlock-forget, page reload or background.

name: seedAdopt

errors: bad request
unknown candidate
Nothing was changed.
Another change to the seed is still waiting. Nothing was changed.

behaviour: Replace the saved seed with a candidate: native alert "Replace this wallet's seed?" (gives up after 120 s as no), then device credential; counters set aside and raised to 1000 short of the furthest range served.

name: seedCandidateForget

errors: bad request

behaviour: Forget a candidate id.

name: seedWipe

errors: Nothing was erased.
Another change to the seed is still waiting. Nothing was changed.

behaviour: Native alert "Delete this wallet's seed?", then device credential; the seed is checked gone before counters move, and a new seed is always made.

name: seedProtection

p1.why: Before P3 the seed is kept under protection none only (SeedVault, P1); device protection and the passcode question come with BiometricPrompt in P3. Asked as the wallet's home screen opens, so a host that connects (P2) meets it.

behaviour: Which protection the person chose: "device" (behind biometric/credential) or "none".

name: seedProtect

errors: bad request
the seed could not be read

behaviour: Move the seed between the two protections. Taking protection off reads the seed from behind it first; written and read back where it is going before the old copy is deleted.

name: scan

errors: Nothing to present the scanner from.
<camera error>

behaviour: Full-screen camera scanner. The prompt is shown only if it is one of native's fixed prompts ("Scan an ecash token", "Scan the mint address"), else blank.

name: previewStart

errors: Nothing to show the camera in.
That pane is too small for a camera (<w>x<h>).
The camera pane must be on screen (...)

behaviour: Live camera laid over the page at a rectangle (CSS px) the page measured: finite, larger than 40x40, inside the web view. Each decoded code is pushed with _liveScan; a refusal is also pushed with _previewRefused.

name: previewStop
behaviour: Stops the live preview.

name: pasteStart

p1.error: Nothing to attach the button to.
p1.why: No native paste control before P3 (BRIDGE.md §4 item 4 decides it there): the page's own PASTE button stays. The page posts this without waiting on the answer, whenever a PASTE button is on screen, which a host that connects (P2) shows.

errors: Nothing to attach the button to.
That is not a place a paste button goes.

behaviour: iOS: a near-invisible UIPasteControl over the page's PASTE button (paste with no system prompt). Rect must be >30x20, <=90% width, <=50% height, inside the view, below its top third. The pasted text (never a seed phrase) is pushed with _pasted.

name: pasteStop

p1.why: Nothing to take down before P3; posted without waiting on the answer, as pasteStart is.

behaviour: Removes the paste control (kept a moment longer, not taking touches, while a paste prompt is up).

name: clipboard

reply.note: the clipboard text, "" when empty or when it is a seed phrase

behaviour: Reads the clipboard, text only; a seed phrase reads as empty (SeedPasteboard.forPage).
timing: Page gives up after 4 s with "".

name: copy

errors: nothing to copy

behaviour: Copy text. sensitive=true (tokens, anything that is money): device-only and expires after 120 s.

name: share

errors: Nothing to share.
Something else is already open.

behaviour: System share sheet with plain text only (no URL item, no link preview fetched).

name: notify

errors: unknown notification kind

behaviour: A local notification. kind is "sent" or "received"; the words are native's ("Payment sent"/"Payment received", titled "Foxy"), no amount. At most one every 3 s.

name: biometric
behaviour: Biometric (or device credential when passcode=true, the screen lock only) for the PIN lock. The reason shown is one of native's ("Unlock Foxy", "Leave POS mode"); anything else shows "Unlock Foxy". A yes is remembered so the following seed read does not ask again.
timing: Page treats no answer in 60 s as "no".

name: openSettings

errors: No settings page to open.
Settings would not open.

behaviour: Opens this app's own system settings page and no other URL (a camera or Bluetooth permission refused once).

name: openCompany

errors: Not one of the listed sites.
The browser would not open.

behaviour: Opens one of four fixed sites by name (cashapp, strike, river, flash) in the system browser, outside Foxy and outside Tor. The page never supplies a URL.

name: haptic
behaviour: A message with no action and no id: { haptic: kind }, dispatched before the action guard. Kinds seen: success, error, warning, pulse, long, heavy, triple; anything else (tap, light) is a light impact. The page rate-limits (one per kind per 1.2 s).

name: username
behaviour: pushToNative(): { username } with no action and no id, on every change, left over from a widget that does not exist. Native dispatch reads it as `.ignored` and does nothing. Android must ignore it the same way (and must not treat it as an unknown action).

name: inboxOpen

errors: No address: Tor is not ready.
No onion address: Tor is not ready.

behaviour: An ephemeral v3 onion address (key made and discarded by Tor) forwarding to a 127.0.0.1 listener, plus a Nostr nprofile listening on up to four relays over Tor, for the payment request on screen. A spare is kept warm. Android (ENG-672): DeliveryBridge.inboxOpen, a port of handleInboxOpen: the open inbox, else the warm spare handed over (and another started), else a new OnionInbox (network/OnionInbox.kt) on a 127.0.0.1 listener with ADD_ONION NEW:ED25519-V3 Flags=DiscardPK,Detach Port=80,127.0.0.1:<port> through tor-android's control link (TorMachine.addOnion; null unless Tor is up). The answer is {"onion"} alone: the Nostr half is LATER (ENG-672 follow-up), and the page takes an answer without nostr as it takes an iPhone whose relays would not listen. While Foxy is put away no address is made and the answer is "No onion address: Tor is not ready."

name: inboxClose
behaviour: End the address (after `hold` seconds, 0..180, if a payment may be on its way) and the Nostr inbox. Android (ENG-672): DeliveryBridge.inboxClose: hold clamped to 0..180 s (a number only), the retiring inbox closed (DEL_ONION) when the hold ends, then the warm spare restarted. Putting Foxy away closes every inbox (the one on screen, the spare and the retiring ones) and drops their answers before Tor parks, as closeInboxForBackground; the bridge going with its page (WebHost.destroy) does the same.

name: inboxAnswer

errors: No payment is waiting on that answer.

behaviour: Answer a payment that arrived (_requestPaid): status 200, 409 or 422 only, 300 characters of text. Android (ENG-670, ENG-672): one table of the answers owed, by key, the onion's and the tap's (InboxAnswers, as FoxyBridge.swift's inboxAnswers with tapAnswerKeys); a key nothing is waiting on is "No payment is waiting on that answer." The answer's JSON is {"ok":true} for 200, else {"error":<text>} written as Apple's JSONSerialization writes it (the slash escaped), the text cut at 300 characters as a person counts them. An onion payment's key is 32 lowercase hex, kept 110 s, and the inbox writes iOS's answer byte for byte (HTTP/1.1 <status> <reason>, Content-Length, Connection: close, Content-Type: application/json when there is a body); its keys go when Foxy is put away. A tap's (_requestPaid(.., "tap")) is kept across Foxy being put away and dropped 30 s after it was pushed, and its status and the JSON's reason become the M6 the payer reads (status 200 with no reason; any other status clamped to 422).

name: onionPost

errors: That is not an onion address.
That payment is too large to send.
Foxy is not connected to Tor.
Their phone could not be reached over Tor.
Tor refused the connection.
Their phone did not answer in time.
The connection to their phone broke.

behaviour: POST a payment to another phone's onion: http:// v3 .onion only, no user/query/fragment, through Tor SOCKS, never the open connection; body <=256 kB, answer cut at 64 kB. timeout in ms, clamped to 3..120 s. Android (ENG-672): DeliveryBridge.onionPost and network/OnionPost.kt: the URL is read by hand (http only as written, a v3 onion host, no user, query or fragment, the path as encoded and printable ASCII, a port that fits), SOCKS5 through Socks5SocketFactory with the circuit label as the login and the onion by name (ATYP 3), then iOS's request byte for byte (POST <path> HTTP/1.1, Host, Content-Type: application/json, Content-Length, Connection: close) and one answer read to the close, cut at 64 kB. Tor only: refused with Route's refusal when Tor is not up, even with CONTINUE WITHOUT TOR on, and (Android) while Route's door is shut as Foxy is put away.

name: nostrSend

errors: That request names no Nostr address.
That payment is too large to send over Nostr.
No relay took the payment: <why>
The payment could not be sent over Nostr.
reply.note: how many relays accepted it, as a decimal string

behaviour: NIP-17/59 gift-wrap the payment for the nprofile in a request and publish to at most five wss relays it names (fallback: damus, nos.lol, primal, minibits), each over Tor on its own circuit; never the open connection.

name: tapReceiveStart

errors: Not something a payer could pay.
That payment is still going through. A moment.

behaviour: Advertise the invoice/payment request on screen over BLE (service UUID only). Payment, quote and stage events come back as _requestPaid(.., "tap"), _tapQuote, _tap. Android (ENG-670, bridge/TapBridge.kt, tap/TapReceiver.kt): a non-empty payload iOS would refuse (TapProtocol.isPayload) is refused with its words and nothing else. Otherwise "ok", and a receiver held since the last tapReceiveStop takes the payload and early flag and stays on the air; one that has handed its offer to a payer is refused "That payment is still going through. A moment." while a payment or change is crossing, keeps that payer's offer and answers "ok" while the payer holds it, and is otherwise retired for a new one. A new receiver (a fresh random service UUID) reports its radio after the reply, as iOS's peripheral manager does: _tap receive stage unsupported (no adapter, or one that cannot advertise), denied (BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE/CONNECT refused; asked by the system's own question if never answered), off, or, once armed, the GATT server up and searching when the advertisement is on the air. The GATT service is iOS's: out (notify), in (write with response), near left and near right (notify), UUIDs SHA-256(label ‖ service)[0..16], a CCCD on each notify door, no encryption or bonding, every read refused; long (prepared) writes are queued per central and taken on the execute; notifications go one at a time, at most MTU - 3 bytes. The advertisement is the service UUID and nothing else: connectable, no name, no TX power, no manufacturer data. Nothing advertises while Foxy is not in front: the activity stopping takes the receiver off the air (and lets it go unless a payment is crossing), and its start puts a new one on the air with what the page last offered. The page asks this by itself on every receive screen (auto-arm); an "Unknown action" reply put UNKNOWN ACTION: TAPRECEIVESTART in the TAP card and was retried every 1.2 s while the screen was up (ENG-656).

name: tapReceiveStop
behaviour: Stop advertising. Android (ENG-670): the receiver is stopped and let go, unless a payment or change is crossing, when it is held (off the air) until that is answered or the result wait (25 s) and 2 s more have passed; "ok" either way.

name: tapPayStart

p1.why: No Bluetooth tap on Android before LATER: every search ends at once, as a stopped one does, and the page backs off its re-listen (up to a minute). A funded wallet's home screen listens with no one acting, so a host that connects (P2) meets it.

errors: Started again.
Stopped.

behaviour: Search for a receiver close enough to be touching and answer its offer plus the four-digit code both phones show; now=true only nudges a search already running and answers "ok". Android (ENG-671): the payer listens (TapPayer: a BLE scan filtered on any service UUID, then iOS's rules for a Foxy advert, the near verdict, the quiet link, the near doors) and answers {payload, code} once the nearest receiver's offer is in. A radio that is off, refused or missing is pushed as _tap({side:"pay",stage}) and the call is not answered, so the page has nothing to re-ask (ENG-658); it is answered "Started again." by the next tapPayStart and "Stopped." by tapPayStop or the page going. now=true answers "ok" at once. Nothing scans while Foxy is put away. The p1 stub is for P1 and P2 hosts only.
timing: Page waits 30 min for a payer to touch.

name: tapSend

errors: There is nothing to hand over.
That phone is no longer connected.
A payment is already going over.
That payment could not be sealed.
That phone went away before it said what became of the payment.
That phone stopped taking the payment.
That phone did not answer after Foxy came back.
Nobody is connected any more.

behaviour: The payment, over the link this tap already holds, <=64 KB. Android (ENG-671): "There is nothing to hand over." for an empty body; "That phone is no longer connected." with no listen or no held link; otherwise the receiver's M6 text as it sealed it, or, when the link went first, why (the TapPayerLink.Handover.Lost words).

name: tapChange

errors: There is no change to send.
That phone is no longer connected.
The payer's phone did not say it kept the change.

behaviour: Change token back to the payer over the same link; resolves when the payer says it kept it (7 s), or late via _tapChangeKeptLate. Android (ENG-670): "There is no change to send." for an empty body, "That phone is no longer connected." with no receiver or no link (nothing sealed), "The payer's phone did not say it kept the change." after 7 s, and a later "kept" as _tapChangeKeptLate.

name: tapChangeKept

errors: No change is waiting to be kept.

behaviour: The payer's page saying it wrote the change down (M8). Android (ENG-671): "ok" and M8 sent when kept is true (nothing is sent for false: the receiver's own 7 s wait answers it); "No change is waiting to be kept." when no _tapChange is waiting.

name: tapAsking
behaviour: The receiver is asking its person about an offline payment (M9). Android (ENG-670): "ok" when M9 went to the payer (the result wait becomes 90 s), "no link" when there is none.

name: tapChangeDue
behaviour: This payment owes change: keep the link. Android (ENG-670): "ok" always; a linked receiver is held (busy) until the payer says it kept the change or goes.

name: tapQuote

errors: That phone is no longer connected.

behaviour: Payer's price quote (M10). Android (ENG-671): "ok" when M10 was sealed and sent over the held link, else "That phone is no longer connected."

name: tapTerms

errors: That phone is no longer connected.

behaviour: Receiver agreeing the price (M11). Android (ENG-670): "ok" when M11 was sealed and sent to the payer, else "That phone is no longer connected."

name: tapPayStop
behaviour: Stop searching/connecting; a waiting tapPayStart is answered with the error "Stopped.". Android (ENG-671): "ok" always; the listen and its link let go (a word still going out goes first).

name: bluetoothAsk
behaviour: First-install screen: put the OS Bluetooth permission question up, answer the state (also pushed to window.__foxyBluetoothAnswer). Scans and advertises nothing. Android (ENG-670, bridge/TapBridge.kt): the system's question for BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT (API 31+; API 28-30 has them at install), never BLUETOOTH_SCAN or location. The state, read once the question is answered: no Bluetooth adapter, or one that is on and cannot advertise (BluetoothAdapter.isMultipleAdvertisementSupported false), is "unsupported" and nothing is asked; a permission refused is "denied"; the adapter off or turning off is "off"; on is "allowed"; one turning on is waited for, and "unknown" after 60 s with no state. Native pushes window.__foxyBluetoothAnswer(state) and then answers state, in iOS's order, so the page writes foxy.bt.asked and closes the screen. A reply without the push left the screen up for good (ENG-656): the page leaves only on the push, and every later APPROVE returns early on `asking`.

name: shakeStart
behaviour: While set, a shake is pushed as _tap({side:"receive",stage:"shake"}). Android (ENG-670): the accelerometer is listened to only while set and Foxy is in front; two jolts of 1.6 g or more within 0.6 s are a shake, then 1.2 s of quiet (tap/Motion.kt ShakeDetector). Idempotent, "ok".

name: shakeStop
behaviour: Clears the shake flag. Android (ENG-670): and lets the accelerometer go. Idempotent, "ok".

name: cardBegin

errors: <CardLinkError words>

behaviour: Open the NFC session with one printable line (<=120 chars) of the page's text; answers when a card is there. One session at a time. Android (ENG-667): bridge/CardBridge.kt over a flashcard/CardLink: on a phone with NFC, reader mode (NfcAdapter.enableReaderMode, NFC-A/B, the NDEF check skipped) with Foxy's own card sheet over the page (Android has no system one: "Ready to Scan", the line, Cancel), on the resumed activity only; in a debug build with no NFC (the emulator), or started with the FoxyCardSim extra, the getfoxy/card simulator over loopback (SimCardLink, ports 47431-47434). The sheet waits 60 s for a card ("the session timed out"); Cancel or Back is "the session was cancelled"; no NFC adapter, or NFC switched off, is "NFC is not available on this phone". With no line from the page the sheet says "Hold the card to the back of the phone" (iOS: the top). Foxy put away while the sheet waits ends it "Foxy was put away" (the begin answered "the session was cancelled"); with a card in hand the card is lost.

name: cardSend

errors: That is not a command for a card.
That is not a command Foxy sends to a card.
<CardLinkError words>

behaviour: One APDU (hex) and its answer. Only SELECT of Foxy's own applet AID (F0 46 4F 58 59 43 41 52 44 01), then only that applet's 31 instructions (CardGate.instructions, CLA B0): 01, 10, 11, 13-1A, 20, 22-26, 30-32, 34-37, 40-45, 51. 1A (GET_DLEQ, card software 1.20) reads back the mint's NUT-12 proof a card keeps with an unspent piece, two places per command; 30 with P1 = 1 (LOAD_PROOF) writes a piece with its proof, 96 more bytes of data (e, s, r), still a short APDU. 12, 33 and 50, which the applet has, stay out. Never logged: one carries the PIN. Android (ENG-667): flashcard/CardGate.kt is CardGate.swift's 31 byte for byte (CardGateTest also holds it to the page's CARD_INS, both ways, and tries every class, instruction and P1/P2). SET_TAG (52, card software 1.19) is not carried, as CardGate.swift at the pin does not carry it, though the card's FOXY-CARD-SPEC.md section 7 (docs/FOXY-CARD-SPEC.md:1070-1072) says a phone's gate should. That section's list is stale against iOS in ten more: 17, 18, 19, 22-26, 35 and 51 (RESET_CARD) are carried here and by CardGate.swift, and the page sends them, but section 7 does not name them. All eleven are for getfoxy/iOS and getfoxy/card to settle together; Android follows iOS. The command is carried over IsoDep (10 s for an answer) or the simulator's "apdu HEX"; an answer under two bytes, a dropped card or the simulator's "gone" is "the tag was lost" with a `_card` lost push, and nothing more is carried until cardAgain finds a card and the applet is chosen again.

name: cardSay
behaviour: Change the line on the NFC sheet. Android (ENG-667): the line on Foxy's card sheet (CardGate.line: one printable line, 120 characters), and a `_card` say push; "ok" with or without a session.

name: cardAgain

errors: <CardLinkError words>

behaviour: The card left part way: look for it again; the applet must be selected again. Android (ENG-667): reader mode is turned off and on again, so a card still in the field is found afresh (iOS: restartPolling), with a new 60 s wait; the sheet shows the page's line ("Hold the card here again" with none). No session: "the session was cancelled".

name: cardEnd
behaviour: Close the sheet with a word or a reason. Android (ENG-667): a tick and the word (1.2 s), or the reason in red (2.4 s), then the sheet goes; reader mode off and the card let go. A sheet still waiting for a card is answered "the session was cancelled". "ok" with or without a session.

name: cardOwnerKey

errors: bad request
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: The P-256 owner PUBLIC key (04||X||Y hex) derived from the seed for one card (its 33-byte compressed key, hex). Android (ENG-666): SeedBridge.cardOwnerKey on the seed executor, refused "bad request" before the seed is read for anything but a 66-hex compressed key; the same key, byte for byte, as an iPhone restored from the same words (app/src/test CardOwnerTest, the iOS tests/fixtures/card-owner-vectors.json). P-256 through the platform's JCA only.

name: cardOwnerSign

errors: bad request
no seed
the seed could not be read

behaviour: ECDSA P-256 DER signature over "FoxyCard/"+label, nonce, value for one of six labels (change-pin, set-limit, set-owner, set-card, load, reset), each with its value shape. Android (ENG-666): SeedBridge.cardOwnerSign on the seed executor; the six labels and their value shapes are CardOwner.Label, and anything else (lock, tag, time, a bad nonce or value) is "bad request" before the seed is read. Signatures verify against the key cardOwnerKey answers, as iOS's do.

name: cardTime

errors: The clock on this phone is not a time a card can be told.

behaviour: The phone clock (u32 seconds) signed by the INTERIM time key built into the app, for cards of software <=1.14. Android (ENG-666): FoxyBridge answers it with InterimCardTime, iOS's interim key pair byte for byte, over "FoxyCard/time" and the four-byte time. A card of software 1.15 and on takes block headers instead, which the page fetches itself over mintRequest and sends with cardSend; nothing of that is native's.

name: _scanResult
behaviour: The one reply path for every action with an id. Exactly one of text/error is non-null. Each argument is a JSON string literal (JSONSerialization of [value], brackets dropped), so a scanned string cannot break out. An id the page no longer waits for is ignored by the page.
timing: Async, on the main thread. Late replies after the page's own timeout are dropped by the page.

name: _privacy
behaviour: Route snapshot on every Tor, Orbot or network change (and once at start without Tor). The page whitelists these fields.

name: _captured
behaviour: Screen recording/mirroring started or stopped: the page hides the seed and secrets while it lasts.

name: _screenshot
behaviour: A screenshot was taken (cannot be stopped on iOS).

name: _previewRefused
behaviour: previewStart was refused (as well as its error reply).

name: _liveScan
behaviour: A code the live preview decoded.

name: _pasted
behaviour: Text pasted through the paste control; a seed phrase arrives as "".

name: _putAway
behaviour: The app went to the background: the page starts its small-change top-up. Native then polls _tidying and Route.out every 0.25 s and keeps Tor up for up to 20 s while money moves, 3 s for other requests, then shuts the door.

name: _tidying
behaviour: Read by native (evaluateJavaScript with a result) while putting away: true while the change top-up is waiting or with the mint.

name: _resumed
behaviour: Back from the background after `away` whole seconds (0 for focus loss without backgrounding). Sent after Tor is told (torResumed) and __foxyUptime is pushed.

name: __foxyUptime
behaviour: Monotonic device uptime, for the PIN back-off clock (22-screen-lock.js). Pushed on didFinish and on every return. Android: SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()/1000.

name: deepLink
behaviour: DEBUG BUILDS ONLY: foxy://receive?amt=50&unit=sat&rail=cashu rebuilt from a whitelist (home, receive, send, token, nfc, split) into the page's own hash. foxy://card (since getfoxy/iOS 9832f7d) sets no hash and takes no parameters: it is a card tap said by hand, delivered as `_cardTapped` (CardTapDelivery). Release registers no scheme and has no handler; the page reads the hash only where FOXY_DEBUG is set. Android (web/DeepLink.kt): foxy://card is recognised and handed to MainActivity's CardTapDelivery, as a card's own address is (ENG-668); nothing of the link reaches the page. The card's https address is not a deep link (see `_cardTapped`).

name: _requestPaid
behaviour: A payment arrived for the request on screen (onion inbox, Nostr inbox with answerId "", or a tap with "tap"). The page redeems it and answers with inboxAnswer. Android: pushed with a fresh 32-hex answer key for a payment posted to an onion inbox (DeliveryBridge, ENG-672), and as `_requestPaid(body, key, "tap")` the moment a tap payment has crossed the link (TapBridge, ENG-670). Not yet the Nostr form (answerId "", the ENG-672 follow-up).

name: _tapQuote
behaviour: M10 arrived on the receiver. Android (ENG-670): pushed with the payer's text as it opened.

name: _tapChange
behaviour: Change arrived on the payer; it answers with tapChangeKept. Android (ENG-671): pushed with the token as it opened, for the listen that made the link; the answer is tapChangeKept.

name: _tapTerms
behaviour: M11 arrived on the payer. Android (ENG-671): pushed with the receiver's text as it opened.

name: __foxyBluetoothAnswer
behaviour: The Bluetooth question was answered (defined by the gate's first-install screen). Android (ENG-670): pushed with the state bluetoothAsk answers (allowed, denied, off, unsupported or unknown) on every bluetoothAsk, before its reply; "unsupported" on a phone with no Bluetooth LE peripheral, as ENG-656 answered on every phone.

name: _turned
behaviour: Device turned portrait/upside-down (the receive screen turns itself for the payer across the table). Android (ENG-670): OrientationEventListener while Foxy is in front (the activity stays portrait): pushed each time the phone comes to portrait (false) or upside down (true), within 30° of each; face up, face down and landscape leave it as it was (tap/Motion.kt TurnDetector).

name: _tapChangeKeptLate
behaviour: The payer said it kept the change after tapChange had already answered. Android (ENG-670): pushed once, for a "kept" that comes after tapChange's 7 s.

name: _tap
behaviour: Tap progress. side receive|pay; stage one of searching, far, connecting, linked, sending, receiving, code, asking, gone, shake, nearby, version, off, denied, unsupported. code only for four digits (stage code), edge left|right only with nearby, pct 0-100 only with sending or receiving. Android (ENG-670): the receive side, as iOS's TapReceiver says it: off/denied/unsupported for the radio, searching when on the air, nearby (edge) and far for payers on the near doors, connecting at a payer's first word, code with the four digits, receiving (pct) for a large payment, gone, version, and shake while shake to TAP is armed. A phone with no Bluetooth LE peripheral says {side:"receive",stage:"unsupported"} once per receiver, after the reply to the tapReceiveStart that made it (ENG-656). The pay side (ENG-671), as iOS's TapPayer says it: off/denied/unsupported for the radio (the listen goes on), nearby (edge: this screen's) and far for a receiver near enough to be told about, connecting when the verdict picks one, gone then searching when that link comes to nothing, linked with the offer, sending (pct) for a large payment, asking while a person decides (M9), and version.

name: _card
behaviour: NFC session progress: stage connected|say|end|lost. Android (ENG-667): pushed by CardBridge through CardGate.progressScript (the text cut to a line and quoted as JSON, `<` `>` `&` and every control escaped) only while the link is the session in hand: connected ("Reading the card") when a card answers, say on cardSay, end when the page closes it, lost when the card leaves mid-command, the wait runs out, the sheet is cancelled or Foxy is put away with a card in hand.

name: _cardTapped
behaviour: A Foxy card was held to the phone (its NDEF address https://getfoxy.io/card, CardAddress), or foxy://card in a debug build. Nothing of the address is passed. The page decides by its screen (`cardTapRule`): act on a home-like screen (opens the Flashcard screen and the card sheet), keep for up to 60 s while locked or starting, ignore anywhere a payment is in progress. The evaluated value is the page's answer: the JS value true once the app has registered it on the wallet (after the lock is decided), anything else means not yet. Native asks again every 0.3 s and gives up 60 s after the latest address arrived (an address that arrives while one waits is the same tap and renews the 60 s); never while the splash or app-switcher cover is up, never after a return before `_resumed` has been told, and never while the page's process is gone: after it ends (pageGone) nothing is asked until the reload has finished (pageLoaded); told once per tap. Set by the app (index.html), not declared in foxy-wallet.js. Android (ENG-668), in every build: CardTapActivity, an invisible door (Theme.NoDisplay, no history, no Recents entry, a task of its own), filters Android's tag dispatch (NDEF_DISCOVERED) and links (VIEW, BROWSABLE, autoVerify false until getfoxy.io publishes an assetlinks.json for the release key) for exactly https://getfoxy.io/card, never MainActivity: flashcard/CardTapRoute.kt starts a new page when none is alive, hands the tap to the page when MainActivity is the top of its task (singleTop, onNewIntent, a one-shot extra with nothing of the address), and drops it while anything is over the page (a seed screen, the scanner, the screen-lock confirmation), as iOS ignores a tap while anything is up, so a card never makes a second page; flashcard/CardTapIntake.kt holds each to flashcard/CardAddress.kt (the iOS rules byte for byte) and drops an intent replayed from Recents, an address while the page has a card session open, and one within 3 s of reader mode going off (the card just read, still resting on the phone): a card being read never re-opens the Flashcard screen. flashcard/CardTapDelivery.kt is the iOS state machine (0.3 s, 60 s from the latest address, once), per MainActivity: the cover is the splash (Android has no app-switcher cover, FLAG_SECURE), the return is told by PutAway after `_resumed`, pageGone is onRenderProcessGone and pageLoaded onPageFinished. The page's answer is read with evaluateJavascript, with no timer on it, as on iOS: a page slow to answer is not asked again, so `_cardTapped()` is never queued twice; a question out to a page whose process ended is forgotten (pageGone) and the reloaded page is asked.
timing: Retried every 0.3 s until the page answers true; given up 60 s after the latest address arrived; a tap while one waits renews it (CardTapDelivery.retryAfter, lapse; cardTapped sets since = now() on every tap, Foxy/Flashcard/CardTapDelivery.swift:64-67). The page keeps a tap it cannot act on yet for up to 60 s (CARD_TAP_KEEP_MS). Android: the same numbers (CardTapDelivery.LAPSE_MS, RETRY_AFTER_MS), and no timeout on a question, as on iOS.

name: noWebRTC
target: every RTC* constructor defined as undefined, non-writable, non-configurable; document start, ALL frames
behaviour: WebRTC STUN is UDP no request block sees; it is removed before any page script so it cannot leak the IP.

name: noCallout
target: a <style>: no touch callout / user-select outside inputs; document end, main frame
behaviour: Look Up / Translate / Search Web would hand selected text to services on the open network.

name: __foxyClock24
behaviour: The phone's 12/24-hour setting (Android: DateFormat.is24HourFormat).

name: FOXY_DEBUG
behaviour: Debug build marker read synchronously by the page.

name: FOXY_SHOW_WARNING
behaviour: Show the first-launch warning again.

name: consoleSilence
behaviour: Release builds silence the page console except console.error. Note: mirrorConsole() still forwards log/warn/error to the `log` action in every build.

name: __foxyPageHash
behaviour: sha256 of the staged page manifest (= sha256(core/SHA256SUMS)); the drawer shows its first 12 characters so a person can compare with the reviewed commit.
